mathgap.title: Sequential Transfer Application
mathgap.principle: When a statement says 'X gives N items to Y', immediately subtract N from X's current count and add N to Y, using the counts as they exist at that point in the narrative.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a transfer sentence appears in the problem text.
mathgap.example: Treating a transfer as a separate equation linking pre‑transfer and post‑transfer variables, e.g., writing X_before - N = X_after and Y_before + N = Y_after, and then using the wrong version in later statements.

mathgap.title: Signed Interpretation of "has K more than"
mathgap.principle: Interpret 'A has K more than B' as the signed equation A − B = K (or A = B + K), preserving the order of names; do not flip the sign.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When parsing comparative statements of the form 'X has K more than Y'.
mathgap.example: Interpreting 'X has K more than Y' as B − A = K, swapping the direction of the equation.

mathgap.title: Signed Equality for Difference Statements
mathgap.principle: For statements like 'The number of items that A has more than B is equal to the difference between the number of items that C and D have', translate to the signed equation (A − B) = (C − D), preserving the order on both sides.
mathgap.example: Treating the equality as |A − B| = |C − D|, i.e., using absolute values and losing sign information.

mathgap.title: Current‑Count Constraint for "has N"
mathgap.principle: A statement 'X has N items' fixes X's count at that point in the narrative, after any earlier transfers have been applied; it does not refer to an initial count if the statement appears later.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When parsing a direct count statement.
mathgap.example: Assuming 'X has N' always refers to the initial count, ignoring earlier transfers that may have already changed X's amount.

mathgap.title: Iterative Substitution and Propagation
mathgap.principle: Whenever a variable's value becomes known, substitute it into all pending equations, simplify them, and propagate the information to solve for further variables.
mathgap.when_to_apply: After each new assignment or equation resolution.
mathgap.example: Leaving a known value unused in later equations, causing the system to remain under‑determined.

mathgap.title: Consistency Check After Solving
mathgap.principle: After assigning values to all variables, verify each original statement—including transfers, direct counts, and difference equations—to ensure no contradictions remain.
mathgap.when_to_apply: After solving the system, before producing the final answer.
mathgap.example: Accepting a solution that violates a given transfer, such as a giver ending with a negative count.

mathgap.title: Chronological Evaluation of Comparative Statements
mathgap.principle: Interpret comparative and difference statements using the counts as they exist at that point in the narrative, after any earlier transfers have been applied.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When processing any statement that compares counts, ensure all prior transfers have been applied first.
mathgap.example: Evaluating a 'has K more than' statement using a person's count before a preceding transfer, leading to an incorrect equation.

mathgap.title: Query‑Focused Subsystem Extraction
mathgap.principle: Identify the subset of equations and statements that involve the queried person directly or through other variables, and solve only that subsystem, ignoring unrelated statements.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Before solving, isolate the relevant part of the system based on the final question.
mathgap.example: Attempting to solve the entire large system, including many irrelevant variables, which increases the chance of error.

mathgap.title: Distinct Name Disambiguation
mathgap.principle: Treat each unique name as a separate variable, even if names differ by only a single character; avoid conflating similarly spelled names.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When parsing the list of individuals and building the variable set.
mathgap.example: Merging 'Alpha' and 'Alph' into a single variable, causing incorrect equations.

mathgap.title: Preserve Order in "Difference Between" Phrases
mathgap.principle: When parsing a phrase like 'the difference between the number of items that A and B have', keep the order as A − B, not B − A, and do not take the absolute value.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When handling difference‑equality statements that use the phrase 'difference between'.
mathgap.example: Swapping A and B, interpreting the phrase as B − A, which reverses the sign of the intended difference.

mathgap.description: Swapped direction in "has K more than"
mathgap.why_it_happens: Model tends to read the phrase as 'B is K more than A' due to natural‑language bias.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Remember that 'A has K more than B' means A − B = K; keep the order of names as they appear.

mathgap.why_it_happens: Model assumes the word 'difference' refers only to magnitude, ignoring sign.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Preserve sign and order; treat 'difference between' as a signed subtraction, not an absolute value.

mathgap.description: Ignoring the chronological order of transfers
mathgap.why_it_happens: Model treats transfers as separate constraints rather than immediate updates, so later statements use outdated counts.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Apply each transfer immediately when encountered, then evaluate later statements with the updated counts.

mathgap.description: Treating "has N" as an initial count regardless of position
mathgap.why_it_happens: Model assumes all direct‑count statements refer to the starting state, ignoring earlier events that may have changed the count.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Interpret 'X has N' as fixing X's count at that point in the narrative, after any earlier transfers.

mathgap.description: Assuming all "more than" differences must be positive
mathgap.why_it_happens: Model interprets the phrase 'more than' as implying a strict inequality A > B.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Allow signed differences; the algebraic relation may be negative if the context dictates, as long as the equation holds.
